**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [6E10 / 4G8 + Alexa Fluor 647, Congo red + Alexa Fluor 568]  
**Justification:** The scientific goal requires deep, uniform labeling of Aβ plaques throughout the intact 5XFAD mouse brain with two orthogonal, target-specific strategies for validation. iDISCO+ is an established solvent-based clearing method for whole adult mouse brains (T04 tier) that enables excellent antibody and dye penetration into dense tissue, critical for detecting deep cortical and hippocampal plaques. Although it quenches endogenous fluorescent proteins, this is irrelevant here as labeling relies on exogenous dyes. Alexa Fluor 647 and Alexa Fluor 568 are both highly compatible with iDISCO+, exhibit minimal quenching in organic solvents, and provide far-red/orange emission ideal for deep imaging with low autofluorescence. 6E10/4G8 antibodies specifically recognize human Aβ (present in 5XFAD), while Congo red—when coupled to Alexa Fluor 568 via co-staining or post-binding enhancement—provides a complementary amyloid-binding chemical strategy that validates immunoreactivity. This dual-labeling approach ensures robust, cross-validated detection of Aβ deposits across all brain regions.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Immunolabeling (post-fixation, pre-clearing)  
1.1 Incubation with blocking solution: 20% (vol/vol) DMSO, 0.3 M glycine, 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with primary antibodies: 6E10 (1:500) and 4G8 (1:500) diluted in antibody dilution buffer (10% DMSO, 0.2% Triton X-100, 0.3 M glycine in PBS). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, gentle shaking)  
1.3 Wash with PTwH buffer: 0.2% Tween-20, 10 µg/mL heparin in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours, with 6 buffer changes)  
1.4 Incubation with secondary antibody: anti-mouse IgG conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647 (1:300) in antibody dilution buffer. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, gentle shaking)  
1.5 Wash with PTwH buffer. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours, with 6 buffer changes)  
1.6 Incubation with Congo red staining solution: 0.2% (wt/vol) Congo red in PBS with 0.1% (vol/vol) sodium azide, followed by post-staining enhancement with Alexa Fluor 568-conjugated anti-Congo red antibody (1:200) or direct incubation with pre-conjugated Congo red–Alexa Fluor 568 complex (if available; otherwise use 0.1% Congo red + 10 µM TO-PRO-3 as counterstain alternative is disallowed, so rely on validated Congo red–Alexa Fluor 568 protocol from literature). (Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours)  
1.7 Final wash with PTwH buffer. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours, with 4 buffer changes)  

2 Dehydration  
2.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.5 Incubation with 100% methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.6 Incubation with fresh 100% methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

3 Delipidation  
3.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (prepared by mixing 1 volume 30% H₂O₂ with 5 volumes methanol). (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours, protected from light)  
3.2 Wash with 100% methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Repeat wash with 100% methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Rehydration (reverse methanol series)  
4.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.5 Incubation with PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

5 Dichloromethane (DCM) treatment  
5.1 Incubation with 100% dichloromethane (DCM, anhydrous). (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
5.2 Repeat incubation with fresh 100% DCM. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

6 Refractive Index Matching  
6.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE, Sigma 108014-1KG). (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours, protected from light)  
6.2 Transfer brain to fresh DBE in imaging-compatible glass vial. (Temperature: RT, Time: until imaging)  

7 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
7.1 Store cleared brain immersed in DBE at RT in the dark. (Temperature: RT, Time: up to 2 weeks)  
7.2 Mount sample in DBE-filled imaging chamber compatible with light-sheet or confocal microscopy. (Temperature: RT, Time: immediate imaging)

**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [CD31 (PECAM1)+Alexa Fluor 647, Lectin (凝集素)+Alexa Fluor 488]  
**Justification:** FDISCO is a solvent-based clearing method established for adult mouse brain blocks (5–12 mm), offering strong delipidation power for dense tumor tissue while preserving exogenous fluorophores like Alexa Fluor dyes. It enables deep antibody and lectin penetration—critical for visualizing both tumor-associated and normal brain vasculature in 3D. CD31 (PECAM1) is a well-validated endothelial-specific marker for all blood vessels, including those in glioblastoma; fluorescently conjugated lectin (e.g., *Lycopersicon esculentum* or *Griffonia simplicifolia* isolectin B4) labels functional vasculature with high specificity and complements CD31 by highlighting perfused or intact luminal surfaces. Using two spectrally distinct Alexa Fluor dyes (488 and 647) ensures robust, non-overlapping signal for high-resolution 3D analysis of vascular architecture and tumor–vessel spatial relationships. FDISCO’s compatibility with both Alexa Fluor 488 and 647, along with its rapid processing and high refractive index matching, makes it ideal for light-sheet imaging of GBM invasion patterns.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Bleaching (optional but recommended for pigmented tumor regions)  
2.1 Incubation with chilled 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ + 5 volumes methanol).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration (for immunolabeling)  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.5 Incubation with 100% PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with permeabilization buffer (0.2% Triton X-100, 10% DMSO, 0.3 M glycine in PBS).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with blocking buffer (6% donkey serum, 0.2% Triton X-100, 10% DMSO in PBS).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Primary and Secondary Labeling (combined direct labeling strategy)  
5.1 Incubation with labeling cocktail: 10 μg/mL Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated anti-CD31 (rat IgG2a, clone MEC13.3) + 20 μg/mL Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated *Lycopersicon esculentum* lectin in blocking buffer.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours, gentle shaking)  

6 Post-labeling Washes  
6.1 Wash with PBST (0.2% Tween-20 in PBS), 3 changes.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)  
6.2 Wash with PBS, 2 changes.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)  

7 Dehydration (post-labeling)  
7.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
7.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
7.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
7.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
7.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
7.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

8 Delipidation  
8.1 Incubation with dichloromethane (DCM, anhydrous, ≥99.8%).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours, gentle agitation)  
8.2 Incubation with fresh dichloromethane.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

9 Refractive Index Matching  
9.1 Incubation with benzyl alcohol:benzyl benzoate (BABB, 1:2 vol/vol) until tissue becomes transparent.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
9.2 Transfer to fresh BABB for long-term storage and imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: indefinite)  

10 Imaging Preparation  
10.1 Mount sample in glass-bottom imaging chamber filled with BABB, ensuring no air bubbles.(Temperature: RT, Time: immediate imaging)

**Chosen Method:** MACS  
**Chosen Labeling:** [GFP (内源), MAP2 + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** The scientific goal requires preservation of weak endogenous fluorescent protein signals (e.g., GFP) in sparse neurons while resolving fine dendritic morphology. MACS is an aqueous, non-denaturing clearing method established for 0.5–3 mm brain slices that robustly preserves GFP/YFP/tdTomato fluorescence and supports deep antibody penetration without quenching. It minimizes tissue distortion and is compatible with both endogenous FP and immunolabeling. MAP2 is a well-validated dendritic marker that complements sparse GFP+ neuron labeling by highlighting the full dendritic arbor, enabling accurate 3D reconstruction of branch patterns, length, and local projections. Alexa Fluor 647 is highly photostable, far-red shifted (minimizing crosstalk with GFP), and fully compatible with MACS.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Immunolabeling (post-fixation, pre-clearing)  
1.1 Wash tissue 3 × 30 min in PBS with 0.3% Triton X-100 (PBST). (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 min per wash)  
1.2 Incubate in blocking solution: 5% normal donkey serum (NDS) + 0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.3 Incubate with primary antibody: anti-MAP2 (chicken or rabbit, 1:500) in blocking solution. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
1.4 Wash 5 × 1 hour in PBST. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)  
1.5 Incubate with secondary antibody: anti-host IgG conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647 (1:800) in blocking solution. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
1.6 Wash 5 × 1 hour in PBST, then 2 × 30 min in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: as indicated)  

2 Tissue Optical Clearing  
2.1 Incubation with MACS-R0 (20 vol% N-methylnicotinamide (MXDA), 15% w/v sorbitol in PBS, pH 7.4). (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with MACS-R1 (40 vol% MXDA, 30% w/v sorbitol in PBS). (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with MACS-R2 (40 vol% MXDA, 50% w/v sorbitol in PBS). (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Refractive Index Matching and Storage  
3.1 Transfer sample to imaging chamber filled with MACS-R2 for immediate imaging. (Temperature: RT, Time: as needed for acquisition)  
3.2 For long-term storage and re-imaging: keep sample immersed in MACS-R2 at 4 ℃ in the dark, sealed to prevent evaporation. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: up to 6 months with stable fluorescence)  
3.3 Prior to re-imaging, equilibrate sample in fresh MACS-R2 at RT for 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)

**Chosen Method:** MACS  
**Chosen Labeling:** [GFP (内源), MAP2 + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** The scientific goal requires preservation of weak endogenous fluorescent protein signals (e.g., GFP) in 3 mm mouse brain blocks over long-term storage, while complementing sparse neuronal morphology with a structural dendritic marker. MACS is an aqueous, refractive-index-tunable clearing method established for thick brain slices (0.5–3 mm), fully compatible with GFP and other FPs, causes minimal tissue distortion, and supports deep antibody penetration. Among pan-neuronal structural markers, MAP2 specifically labels dendrites and soma—ideal for reconstructing dendritic arbors of sparse reporter neurons—and is compatible with Alexa Fluor 647, which remains stable in MACS and resists long-term quenching. This dual-labeling strategy preserves the native reporter signal while adding high-contrast, durable dendritic detail for 3D morphological mapping.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Immunolabeling (post-fixation, pre-clearing)  
1.1 Incubation with blocking solution: 10% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum, 0.3% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with primary antibody: anti-MAP2 (chicken or rabbit, 1:500) in antibody dilution buffer (1% NDS, 0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS) (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours with gentle agitation)  
1.3 Wash with PBST (0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS): 3 × 1 hour each (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)  
1.4 Incubation with secondary antibody: Alexa Fluor 647–conjugated anti-host IgG (1:500) in antibody dilution buffer (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours with gentle agitation)  
1.5 Wash with PBST: 3 × 1 hour each (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)  

2 Tissue Optical Clearing  
2.1 Incubation with MACS-R0 (20 vol% MXDA, 15% w/v sorbitol in PBS, pH 7.4) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with MACS-R1 (40 vol% MXDA, 30% w/v sorbitol in PBS, pH 7.4) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with MACS-R2 (40 vol% MXDA, 50% w/v sorbitol in PBS, pH 7.4) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Refractive Index Matching and Long-Term Storage  
3.1 Transfer tissue to final RI-matching solution: MACS-R2 stored in light-protected glass vial sealed with parafilm (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: indefinite; stable for ≥6 months)  
3.2 Prior to imaging after storage: equilibrate sample in fresh MACS-R2 at RT for 2 hours to restore optical homogeneity (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)

**Chosen Labeling:** [GFP (内源), MAP2 + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** The problem requires preservation of weak endogenous fluorescent protein signals (e.g., GFP/YFP) over long-term storage (6 months) and high-fidelity 3D reconstruction of sparse neuronal morphology, including dendritic arborization. MACS is an aqueous-based clearing method established for 0.5–3 mm brain slices, fully compatible with endogenous GFP and exogenous Alexa Fluor dyes, causes minimal tissue distortion, and supports deep antibody penetration—critical for labeling pan-neuronal dendritic markers like MAP2 to complement sparse genetic reporters. Unlike solvent-based methods (e.g., iDISCO+), MACS avoids FP quenching and hazardous reagents, enabling stable signal retention during extended storage. MAP2 provides robust dendritic skeleton labeling without interfering with endogenous GFP, allowing dual-channel analysis of specific reporter neurons and their full dendritic architecture.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Immunolabeling (post-fixation, pre-clearing)  
1.1 Incubation with blocking solution: 5% (vol/vol) normal goat serum, 0.3% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with primary antibody: anti-MAP2 (chicken or mouse monoclonal, 1:500 dilution) in blocking solution (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
1.3 Wash with PBST (0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS): 3 changes, 1 hour each (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with secondary antibody: Alexa Fluor 647–conjugated anti-host IgG (1:800 dilution) in blocking solution (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
1.5 Wash with PBST: 3 changes, 1 hour each (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 1 hour)  

2 Tissue Optical Clearing  
2.1 Incubation with MACS-R0 (20 vol% MXDA, 15% w/v sorbitol in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with MACS-R1 (40 vol% MXDA, 30% w/v sorbitol in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with MACS-R2 (40 vol% MXDA, 50% w/v sorbitol in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Refractive Index Matching and Long-Term Storage  
3.1 Transfer cleared tissue into fresh MACS-R2 in airtight imaging-compatible glass vial (e.g., with PTFE-lined cap) (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: indefinite)  
3.2 Store at 4 ℃ in the dark for up to 6 months; no medium change required  

4 Pre-Imaging Equilibration (prior to light-sheet or confocal imaging)  
4.1 Equilibrate sample in fresh MACS-R2 at RT for 1 hour before mounting (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

model_response:
**Chosen Method:** MACS  
**Chosen Labeling:** [GFP (内源), MAP2 + Alexa Fluor 488]  
**Justification:** The scientific goal requires preservation of extremely weak endogenous fluorescent protein signal (e.g., GFP) over 6 months, which rules out solvent-based methods like iDISCO+ or uDISCO that quench or destabilize FPs. Among aqueous, FP-compatible clearing methods established for 3 mm brain blocks (T02_THICK_SLICE_0P5_3MM), MACS offers superior balance: it preserves endogenous GFP/YFP/tdTomato fluorescence, enables deep penetration of antibodies into dense tissue, minimizes morphological distortion, and uses low-toxicity reagents suitable for long-term archival. For structural补全 of sparse neurons, MAP2 is a well-validated dendritic marker that labels proximal and distal dendrites without labeling axons, complementing weak somatic GFP signal to enable accurate reconstruction of dendritic arborization, branch points, and local projection patterns. Alexa Fluor 488 is fully compatible with MACS and spectrally separable from common red reporters while matching GFP excitation/emission for co-imaging; its photostability supports long-term storage. DAPI/Hoechst are avoided per marker-level cautions for MAP2.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Immunolabeling (post-fixation, pre-clearing)  
1.1 Incubation with blocking solution: 5% (vol/vol) normal goat serum, 0.3% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with primary antibody: anti-MAP2 (mouse or rabbit monoclonal, 1:500 dilution) in antibody dilution buffer (1% NGS, 0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS) (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
1.3 Wash with PBST (0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS): 3 changes, 1 hour each (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)  
1.4 Incubation with secondary antibody: Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-host IgG (1:800 dilution) in antibody dilution buffer (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
1.5 Wash with PBST: 3 changes, 1 hour each (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)  

2 Tissue Optical Clearing

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [NeuN (RBFOX3) + Alexa Fluor 488, MAP2 + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** The sample is a 5 mm thick, fixed human cortical slice from dense clinical tissue with high lipid/myelin content, requiring a clearing method with strong delipidation power and deep antibody penetration. iDISCO+ is established for this tissue tier (T09_HUMAN_DENSE_CLINICAL_BLOCK), provides rapid and effective clearing of large, lipid-rich brain samples, and supports robust immunolabeling with synthetic fluorophores. Endogenous fluorescent proteins are not used; instead, two mature neuron-specific structural markers—NeuN (nuclear) and MAP2 (somatic/dendritic)—are co-labeled with spectrally distinct, iDISCO+-compatible Alexa Fluor dyes (488 and 647). This dual-target strategy enables reliable identification of mature neuronal somata through colocalization of nuclear (NeuN) and cytoplasmic (MAP2) signals, improving cell detection accuracy in dense 3D tissue for quantitative spatial analysis across cortical layers and perilesional zones.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Bleaching (optional for pigmented human tissue)  
2.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes methanol).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBT).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with PBT + 20% (vol/vol) DMSO + 0.3 M glycine.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with PBT + 10% (vol/vol) donkey serum + 0.2% (wt/vol) sodium azide.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Primary Antibody Staining  
5.1 Incubation with anti-NeuN (mouse monoclonal, 1:500) and anti-MAP2 (rabbit polyclonal, 1:500) diluted in PBT + 5% (vol/vol) donkey serum + 0.2% (wt/vol) sodium azide.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, gentle agitation)  

6 Wash  
6.1 Wash with PBT.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour, repeated 6 times over 24 hours)  

7 Secondary Antibody Staining  
7.1 Incubation with donkey anti-mouse Alexa Fluor 488 (1:500) and donkey anti-rabbit Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500) in PBT + 5% (vol/vol) donkey serum + 0.2% (wt/vol) sodium azide.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, gentle agitation)  

8 Wash  
8.1 Wash with PBT.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour, repeated 6 times over 24 hours)  

9 Dehydration (post-staining)  
9.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.6 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

10 Delipidation  
10.1 Incubation with dichloromethane (DCM, anhydrous).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.2 Incubation with dichloromethane (DCM, anhydrous).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

11 Refractive Index Matching  
11.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE, Sigma 108014-1KG).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [NeuN (RBFOX3) + Alexa Fluor 488, MAP2 + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** The sample is a 5 mm thick, lipid- and myelin-rich human cortical slice—classified as high-clearing-difficulty dense clinical tissue. iDISCO+ is an established organic solvent–based method for this tissue tier, offering strong delipidation power essential for deep antibody penetration and uniform clearing across the full thickness. Although it quenches endogenous fluorescent proteins, our labeling strategy uses robust, target-specific primary antibodies against mature neuron markers NeuN (nuclear pan-neuronal marker) and MAP2 (dendritic cytoskeletal marker), conjugated to photostable Alexa Fluor dyes compatible with iDISCO+. This dual-target approach enables accurate 3D neuron identification (via NeuN) and morphological context (via MAP2), supporting cell counting, laminar mapping, and local density analysis. Nuclear counterstains like DAPI are avoided per compatibility cautions for these neuronal markers.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Bleaching (optional but recommended for human tissue with potential pigments)  
2.1 Incubation with chilled 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in 100% methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ + 5 volumes methanol).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBT).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with PBT + 20% (vol/vol) DMSO + 0.3 M glycine.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with PBT + 10% (vol/vol) DMSO + 6% (wt/vol) donkey serum.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Primary Antibody Staining  
5.1 Incubation with anti-NeuN (mouse monoclonal, 1:500) and anti-MAP2 (rabbit polyclonal, 1:500) diluted in PBT + 10% (vol/vol) DMSO + 6% (wt/vol) donkey serum.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, with gentle agitation)  

6 Wash  
6.1 Incubation with PBT + 10% (vol/vol) DMSO.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
6.2 Repeat wash step 6.1 two more times, changing solution daily.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours each)  

7 Secondary Antibody Staining  
7.1 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 488–conjugated donkey anti-mouse IgG (1:500) and Alexa Fluor 647–conjugated donkey anti-rabbit IgG (1:500) in PBT + 10% (vol/vol) DMSO + 6% (wt/vol) donkey serum.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days, with gentle agitation)  

8 Post-staining Wash  
8.1 Incubation with PBT + 10% (vol/vol) DMSO.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
8.2 Repeat wash step 8.1 two more times, changing solution daily.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours each)  

9 Dehydration (pre-clearing)  
9.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

10 Delipidation  
10.1 Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) in 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.3 Repeat step 10.2 once with fresh DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

11 Refractive Index Matching  
11.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
11.2 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) DBE in glass vial suitable for imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: ≥12 hours, until optically transparent)  

12 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
12.1 Store sample immersed in DBE at RT in light-protected container until imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: indefinite for short-term; replace DBE weekly for long-term)  
12.2 Mount directly in DBE-compatible imaging chamber for light-sheet or confocal microscopy without additional steps.

**Chosen Method:** FOCM  
**Chosen Labeling:** [GFP (内源), MAP2 + Alexa Fluor 568]  
**Justification:** The scientific goal requires preservation of endogenous fluorescent protein signal (e.g., GFP/YFP from sparse neuronal labeling) and high-fidelity visualization of dendritic shafts and spines in 500 μm brain slices within a single day. FOCM is an aqueous, fast, FP-compatible clearing method established for thin brain slices (≤500 μm), with minimal morphological distortion and excellent preservation of GFP and Alexa Fluor dyes. MAP2 is a well-established dendritic marker that labels the somatodendritic compartment robustly, enabling clear delineation of dendritic arbors and spine-bearing segments when combined with endogenous GFP-labeled neurons. Alexa Fluor 568 is compatible with FOCM and provides strong, photostable signal for dendritic backbone without spectral overlap with GFP.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Immunostaining (Perform before clearing)  
1.1 Permeabilization and blocking: Incubate slices in blocking buffer (0.5% Triton X-100, 5% normal goat serum in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Primary antibody incubation: Incubate with anti-MAP2 mouse monoclonal antibody (1:500 in blocking buffer) (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  
1.3 Wash: Rinse 3 × 30 min in PBS with 0.1% Tween-20 (PBST) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1.5 hours total)  
1.4 Secondary antibody incubation: Incubate with Alexa Fluor 568-conjugated goat anti-mouse IgG (1:800 in blocking buffer) (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)  
1.5 Final wash: Rinse 3 × 30 min in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1.5 hours total)  

2 Tissue Optical Clearing with FOCM  
2.1 Incubation with FOCM Clearing Solution A (8% (wt/vol) N-methylnicotinamide, 17% (wt/vol) urea, 20% (wt/vol) sucrose, 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 2 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with FOCM Clearing Solution B (25% (wt/vol) N-methylnicotinamide, 25% (wt/vol) urea, 30% (wt/vol) sucrose, 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 2 hours)  

3 Refractive Index Matching and Mounting  
3.1 Incubation with FOCM RI Matching Solution (63% (wt/vol) iodixanol in PBS, final RI ≈ 1.38–1.40) (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.2 Mount slices in FOCM RI Matching Solution in glass-bottom imaging dishes or between coverslips with spacer (Temperature: RT, Time: immediate imaging)

**Chosen Method:** MACS  
**Chosen Labeling:** [GFP (内源), MAP2 + Alexa Fluor 568]  
**Justification:** The scientific goal requires preservation of endogenous fluorescent protein signal (e.g., GFP/YFP from sparse neuronal labeling) while complementing with a structural marker to delineate full dendritic arbors for spine density normalization. MACS is an aqueous, fast, and FP-compatible clearing method established for ≤500 μm brain slices, enabling excellent preservation of GFP fluorescence and efficient penetration of antibody-conjugated dyes within 1 day. MAP2 is a well-validated dendritic cytoskeletal marker that labels the entire somatodendritic compartment without labeling axons, making it ideal for reconstructing dendritic length and branching. Alexa Fluor 568 is spectrally distinct from GFP and fully compatible with MACS, allowing dual-channel high-resolution imaging of spines (via GFP) and dendritic backbone (via MAP2-AF568).

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Immunostaining (Perform before clearing)  
1.1 Incubation with blocking solution: 5% (vol/vol) normal goat serum, 0.3% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with primary antibody: anti-MAP2 (chicken or mouse monoclonal, 1:500 dilution) in blocking solution (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 16 hours)  
1.3 Wash with PBS + 0.3% Triton X-100 (3 × 30 minutes) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1.5 hours total)  
1.4 Incubation with secondary antibody: Alexa Fluor 568–conjugated anti-host IgG (1:1000 dilution) in blocking solution (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)  
1.5 Wash with PBS (3 × 30 minutes) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1.5 hours total)  

2 Tissue Optical Clearing  
2.1 Incubation with MACS-R0 (20 vol% MXDA, 15% w/v sorbitol in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with MACS-R1 (40 vol% MXDA, 30% w/v sorbitol in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with MACS-R2 (40 vol% MXDA, 50% w/v sorbitol in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)  

3 Refractive Index Matching and Mounting  
3.1 Incubation with final RI-matching solution: MACS-R2 (same as 2.3) for equilibration (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Mount cleared slice in a glass-bottom imaging dish filled with fresh MACS-R2, covered with a coverslip supported by silicone spacers to avoid compression (Temperature: RT, Time: immediate imaging or storage at 4 ℃ up to 1 week)

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [NeuN (RBFOX3) + Alexa Fluor 488, MAP2 + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** The problem involves dense, fixed human cortical tissue (3 mm thick) with poor antibody penetration using standard aqueous labeling. iDISCO+ is an organic solvent–based clearing method established for T09_HUMAN_DENSE_CLINICAL_BLOCK, offering strong delipidation and deep antibody penetration—critical for uniform labeling throughout 3 mm. Although it quenches endogenous fluorescent proteins, the protocol uses exogenous Alexa Fluor–conjugated antibodies, which are fully compatible with iDISCO+. NeuN (nuclear marker of mature neurons) and MAP2 (dendritic/somatic marker) provide complementary structural confirmation of mature neurons, enhancing reliability of deep-cell identification. Both markers are well-validated in human postmortem brain and compatible with organic clearing when labeled via robust secondary antibodies or directly conjugated primaries. PBS dilution was insufficient for penetration; iDISCO+’s methanol/DCM-based permeabilization enables effective primary/secondary antibody access to deep layers.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Endogenous Peroxidase Quenching (optional but recommended for human tissue)  
2.1 Incubation with chilled 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in 100% methanol.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration (for immunolabeling)  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBT).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

4 Blocking and Primary Antibody Incubation  
4.1 Incubation with blocking solution: PBT + 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum + 0.3 M glycine.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-NeuN (mouse monoclonal, 1:500) + anti-MAP2 (rabbit polyclonal, 1:500) diluted in PBT + 3% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum + 0.02% (wt/vol) sodium azide.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours with gentle agitation)  

5 Washing  
5.1 Incubation with PBT.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.2 Repeat PBT wash 5 times, each with fresh solution.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)  

6 Secondary Antibody Incubation  
6.1 Incubation with secondary antibodies: donkey anti-mouse Alexa Fluor 488 (1:500) + donkey anti-rabbit Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500) in PBT + 3% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum + 0.02% (wt/vol) sodium azide.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours with gentle agitation)  

7 Post-labeling Washes  
7.1 Incubation with PBT.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
7.2 Repeat PBT wash 5 times, each with fresh solution.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)  

8 Dehydration (pre-clearing)  
8.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
8.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
8.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
8.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
8.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
8.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

9 Delipidation  
9.1 Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) in methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.3 Repeat 100% DCM incubation with fresh solution.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

10 Refractive Index Matching  
10.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
10.2 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) DBE in glass vial, protected from light.(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

11 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
11.1 Store sample immersed in DBE at RT in amber glass vial until imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: indefinite)  
11.2 Mount cleared slice in a DBE-filled imaging chamber compatible with light-sheet or confocal microscopy, ensuring no air bubbles.(Temperature: RT, Time: immediate prior to imaging)

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [NeuN (RBFOX3) + Alexa Fluor 488, MAP2 + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** The problem involves dense, fixed human cortical tissue (3 mm thick) with poor antibody penetration using standard aqueous labeling. iDISCO+ is an organic solvent–based clearing method established for T09_HUMAN_DENSE_CLINICAL_BLOCK, offering strong delipidation and deep antibody penetration—critical for uniform labeling across the full thickness. Although it quenches endogenous fluorescent proteins, this is irrelevant here as labeling relies on exogenous antibodies conjugated to compatible fluorophores. Alexa Fluor 488 and 647 are both highly compatible with iDISCO+, photostable, and spectrally separable for dual-channel mature neuron detection: NeuN labels neuronal nuclei (pan-mature neuron), while MAP2 labels dendritic arbors and somata, together providing complementary structural confirmation of mature neurons throughout the depth. This dual-target strategy enhances reliability of deep-cell identification beyond single-marker ambiguity.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Endogenous Peroxidase Quenching (optional but recommended for human tissue)  
2.1 Incubation with chilled 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in 100% methanol (prepared by mixing 1 volume 30% H₂O₂ with 5 volumes methanol).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration (for immunolabeling)  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBST).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with PBST + 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum (NDS) + 0.3 M glycine.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

5 Primary Antibody Staining  
5.1 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-NeuN (mouse monoclonal, 1:500) and anti-MAP2 (rabbit polyclonal, 1:250) diluted in PBST + 5% NDS + 0.02% (wt/vol) sodium azide.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours with gentle agitation)  

6 Wash  
6.1 Incubation with PBST.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.2 Repeat PBST wash 5 times, each with fresh solution.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)  

7 Secondary Antibody Staining  
7.1 Incubation with secondary antibodies: donkey anti-mouse IgG conjugated to Alexa Fluor 488 (1:500) and donkey anti-rabbit IgG conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500), diluted in PBST + 5% NDS + 0.02% sodium azide.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours with gentle agitation)  

8 Post-staining Wash  
8.1 Incubation with PBST.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
8.2 Repeat PBST wash 5 times, each with fresh solution.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)  

9 Dehydration (pre-clearing)  
9.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

10 Delipidation  
10.1 Incubation with dichloromethane (DCM, anhydrous, ≥99.8%).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.2 Incubation with fresh DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

11 Refractive Index Matching  
11.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE, Sigma 108014-1KG).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
11.2 Incubation with fresh 100% DBE for long-term storage or imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: ≥1 hour or until imaging)  

12 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
12.1 Store samples immersed in DBE in glass vials protected from light at RT. Samples are ready for light-sheet or confocal microscopy with oil-immersion or DBE-matched objectives (RI ≈ 1.56).

**Chosen Method:** FOCM  
**Chosen Labeling:** [EGFP (endogenous), MAP2 + Alexa Fluor 568]  
**Justification:** FOCM is an aqueous, fast, and morphology-preserving clearing method established for ≤500 μm brain slices, fully compatible with endogenous fluorescent proteins (e.g., EGFP) and exogenous dyes like Alexa Fluor 568. It achieves sufficient transparency within hours without organic solvents that quench fluorescence or distort fine structures like dendritic spines. The dual-labeling strategy uses endogenous EGFP to label specific neurons (e.g., in Thy1-EGFP-M mice where EGFP fills dendrites and spines) and immunostaining against MAP2—a pan-dendritic marker—to provide a robust dendritic backbone for orientation, segment selection, and spine density normalization per unit dendritic length. This combination enables unambiguous identification of dendritic segments and accurate spine counting while preserving native fluorescence and tissue geometry.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Immunostaining (if not pre-stained)  
1.1 Incubation with blocking solution (5% normal goat serum, 0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS) to reduce non-specific binding. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with primary antibody against MAP2 (1:500 dilution in blocking solution). (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  
1.3 Wash with PBS + 0.3% Triton X-100 (3 × 30 minutes). (Temperature: RT, Time: 1.5 hours total)  
1.4 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 568–conjugated secondary antibody (1:1000 in blocking solution). (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.5 Wash with PBS (3 × 30 minutes). (Temperature: RT, Time: 1.5 hours total)  

2 Tissue Optical Clearing with FOCM  
2.1 Incubation with FOCM Clearing Solution A (8.5% w/v fructose, 8.5% w/v sucrose, 0.5% w/v α-thioglycerol in PBS). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 2 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with FOCM Clearing Solution B (42.5% w/v fructose, 42.5% w/v sucrose, 2.5% w/v α-thioglycerol in PBS). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 3 hours)  

3 Refractive Index Matching and Mounting  
3.1 Incubation with FOCM Imaging Buffer (63% w/v fructose, 10% w/v sucrose, 5% w/v α-thioglycerol in PBS; RI ≈ 1.45). (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.2 Mount sample in FOCM Imaging Buffer between #1.5 coverslips using spacer or imaging chamber suitable for confocal/light-sheet microscopy. (Temperature: RT, Time: immediate imaging or store at 4 ℃ for up to 24 hours)

**Chosen Method:** MACS  
**Chosen Labeling:** [β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) + Alexa Fluor 488, Sox10 + Alexa Fluor 568]  
**Justification:** E12.5 mouse embryos (~8–10 mm) require deep antibody penetration into intact neural tissue while preserving fine neurite morphology and minimizing distortion. MACS is an aqueous, low-toxicity clearing method established for small whole embryos (T03 tier), compatible with both endogenous and antibody-based fluorescence, and maintains tissue geometry—critical for accurate 3D reconstruction of early nerve trajectories. β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) robustly labels all neuronal processes (including cranial/spinal/peripheral nerves), while Sox10 specifically marks neural crest-derived Schwann cell precursors and glial lineages that accompany developing peripheral nerves, enabling dual-channel visualization of axons and their associated support cells. Both primary antibodies are efficiently penetrated in MACS, and Alexa Fluor 488/568 dyes are fully compatible with MACS chemistry without quenching.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Immunolabeling (post-fixation)  
1.1 Wash fixed embryo 3 × 1 hour in PBS with 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBST). (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)  
1.2 Incubate in blocking solution: 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)  
1.3 Incubate with primary antibodies: anti-β-III Tubulin (TUJ1, 1:500) and anti-Sox10 (1:200) in blocking solution. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 72 hours with gentle agitation)  
1.4 Wash thoroughly: 6 × 2 hours in PBST. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours per wash)  
1.5 Incubate with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 488 donkey anti-mouse IgG (1:500) and Alexa Fluor 568 donkey anti-rabbit IgG (1:500) in blocking solution, protected from light. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours with gentle agitation)  
1.6 Wash thoroughly: 6 × 2 hours in PBST, then 2 × 1 hour in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: as indicated)  

2 Tissue Optical Clearing (MACS)  
2.1 Incubation with MACS-R0: 20% (vol/vol) N-methylnicotinamide (MXDA), 15% (wt/vol) sorbitol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with MACS-R1: 40% (vol/vol) MXDA, 30% (wt/vol) sorbitol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with MACS-R2: 40% (vol/vol) MXDA, 50% (wt/vol) sorbitol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Refractive Index Matching and Storage  
3.1 Transfer cleared embryo to imaging chamber filled with MACS-R2 for immediate light-sheet or confocal imaging. (Temperature: RT, Time: imaging within 7 days)  
3.2 For long-term storage, keep sample immersed in MACS-R2 at 4 ℃ in the dark. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: up to 4 weeks without signal degradation)

**Chosen Method:** MACS  
**Chosen Labeling:** [EGFP (endogenous), MAP2 + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** The original TDE protocol failed due to excessive concentration (100% directly), prolonged incubation, and methanol-based fixation—known to damage fine dendritic structures and cause shrinkage. For rapid (<24 h), high-fidelity clearing of 500 μm brain slices with preserved endogenous EGFP and enhanced dendritic skeleton visualization, MACS is optimal: it is aqueous, FP-compatible, minimally distorting, and established for thin brain slices (≤500 μm). EGFP provides sparse neuronal labeling for spine identification, while anti-MAP2 immunostaining with Alexa Fluor 647 complements the dendritic arbor morphology without quenching, enabling accurate spine density normalization per unit dendrite length. MACS supports deep antibody penetration within hours and avoids organic solvents that degrade spines or induce shrinkage.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Rehydration (if methanol-fixed)  
1.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 30 min. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
1.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 30 min. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
1.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 30 min. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
1.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 30 min. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
1.5 Incubation with PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Permeabilization and Blocking  
2.1 Incubation with permeabilization buffer (0.5% Triton X-100, 10% normal goat serum in PBS) for 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

3 Primary Antibody Staining (anti-MAP2)  
3.1 Incubation with anti-MAP2 primary antibody diluted 1:500 in antibody dilution buffer (0.2% Triton X-100, 5% normal goat serum in PBS) for 6 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)  

4 Wash  
4.1 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% Tween-20 (PBT) for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.2 Repeat wash step 4.1 two more times. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour each)  

5 Secondary Antibody Staining (Alexa Fluor 647)  
5.1 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 647–conjugated anti-mouse IgG (or appropriate host-specific) diluted 1:800 in antibody dilution buffer for 4 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)  

6 Final Wash  
6.1 Incubation with PBT for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.2 Repeat wash step 6.1 two more times. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour each)  

7 Optical Clearing with MACS  
7.1 Incubation with MACS-R0 (20 vol% MXDA, 15% w/v sorbitol in PBS) for 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
7.2 Incubation with MACS-R1 (40 vol% MXDA, 30% w/v sorbitol in PBS) for 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
7.3 Incubation with MACS-R2 (40 vol% MXDA, 50% w/v sorbitol in PBS) for 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

8 Refractive Index Matching and Mounting  
8.1 Transfer slice into fresh MACS-R2 for imaging. (Temperature: RT, Time: immediate imaging or storage at 4 ℃ up to 48 h)

**Chosen Method:** MACS  
**Chosen Labeling:** [β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) + Alexa Fluor 488, Sox10 + Alexa Fluor 568]  
**Justification:** The scientific goal requires high-fidelity 3D mapping of early cranial, spinal, and peripheral nerve projections in an intact E12.5 mouse embryo (~8–10 mm). β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) is a well-established pan-neuronal marker that labels all developing axons, enabling comprehensive tracing of nerve trajectories. Sox10 is a lineage-specific transcription factor expressed in neural crest-derived Schwann cell precursors that intimately associate with peripheral nerves at this stage, providing a second, complementary signal to validate nerve identity and distinguish true projections from background or non-neural structures. MACS is selected because it is an aqueous, low-distortion clearing method established for small whole embryos (T03 tier), preserves endogenous fluorescence (though not needed here as labeling is antibody-based), supports deep antibody penetration, and maintains tissue morphology—critical for accurate spatial mapping of fine, early nerve fibers. Both Alexa Fluor 488 and 568 are fully compatible with MACS and offer bright, photostable signals ideal for light-sheet imaging.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Immunolabeling (post-fixation)  
1.1 Wash fixed embryo 3 × 1 hour in PBS with 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBST).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)  
1.2 Incubate in blocking solution: PBST + 5% (vol/vol) normal goat serum + 1% (wt/vol) DMSO.(Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)  
1.3 Incubate with primary antibodies: anti-β-III Tubulin (TUJ1, e.g., BioLegend 801201, 1:500) and anti-Sox10 (e.g., Santa Cruz sc-17343, 1:200) diluted in blocking solution.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 5 days with gentle agitation)  
1.4 Wash thoroughly: 5 × 12 hours in PBST (change buffer every 12 hours).(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours per wash)  
1.5 Incubate with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-mouse IgG (1:500) and Alexa Fluor 568-conjugated anti-rabbit IgG (1:500) in blocking solution, protected from light.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 4 days with gentle agitation)  
1.6 Wash thoroughly: 5 × 12 hours in PBST (protected from light).(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours per wash)  

2 Tissue Optical Clearing (MACS)  
2.1 Incubation with MACS-R0: 20% (vol/vol) N-methylnicotinamide (MXDA), 15% (wt/vol) sorbitol in PBS, pH 7.4.(Temperature: RT, Time: 36 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with MACS-R1: 40% (vol/vol) MXDA, 30% (wt/vol) sorbitol in PBS, pH 7.4.(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with MACS-R2: 40% (vol/vol) MXDA, 50% (wt/vol) sorbitol in PBS, pH 7.4.(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Refractive Index Matching and Storage  
3.1 Transfer embryo to imaging chamber filled with MACS-R2 for immediate light-sheet or confocal imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: imaging within 7 days)  
3.2 For long-term storage, keep sample immersed in MACS-R2 at 4 ℃ in the dark.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: up to 1 month)

**Chosen Labeling:** [β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) + Alexa Fluor 647, PGP9.5 + Alexa Fluor 488]  
**Justification:** The scientific goal requires simultaneous visualization of mature nerve bundles and early neuronal processes throughout the entire E12.5 mouse embryo (~8–10 mm). β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) robustly labels developing and mature neurons, including fine axonal projections, while PGP9.5 provides complementary pan-neuronal labeling of more established fibers, ensuring coverage across developmental stages. Both are target-specific neural markers validated for embryonic peripheral and central nervous systems. MACS is an aqueous, low-shrinkage clearing method established for small whole embryos (T03 tier), preserves Alexa Fluor dyes with high fidelity, enables deep antibody penetration without quenching, and maintains tissue geometry critical for 3D reconstruction of continuous nerve trajectories. Unlike solvent-based methods (e.g., iDISCO+), MACS avoids distortion and is compatible with extended antibody incubations needed for thick samples. The prior failure—due to insufficient washing and short antibody incubation—is addressed by implementing prolonged, temperature-controlled labeling and rigorous post-labeling washes.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Primary Antibody Incubation  
1.1 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-β-III Tubulin (TUJ1, 1:500) and anti-PGP9.5 (1:500) diluted in MACS-A buffer (0.2% Triton X-100, 0.3 M glycine, 20% DMSO, 0.01% NaN₃ in PBS) with gentle agitation. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days)  

2 Washing  
2.1 Wash with MACS-W buffer (0.2% Triton X-100, 0.3 M glycine in PBS) with gentle agitation. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash, repeat 6 times over 24 hours)  

3 Secondary Antibody Incubation  
3.1 Incubation with secondary antibodies: donkey anti-mouse IgG Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500) and donkey anti-rabbit IgG Alexa Fluor 488 (1:500) diluted in MACS-A buffer with 5% normal donkey serum, protected from light, with gentle agitation. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days)  

4 Post-Labeling Washing  
4.1 Wash with MACS-W buffer with gentle agitation. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours per wash, repeat 6 times over 48 hours)  

5 Optional Background Reduction (if residual background persists)  
5.1 Incubation with 0.1% Sudan Black B in 70% ethanol (prepared fresh) with gentle agitation. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
5.2 Wash with 70% ethanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 min)  
5.3 Wash with MACS-W buffer. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

6 Tissue Clearing  
6.1 Incubation with MACS-R0 (20 vol% MXDA, 15% w/v sorbitol in PBS, pH 7.5). (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
6.2 Incubation with MACS-R1 (40 vol% MXDA, 30% w/v sorbitol in PBS, pH 7.5). (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
6.3 Incubation with MACS-R2 (40 vol% MXDA, 50% w/v sorbitol in PBS, pH 7.5). (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

7 Refractive Index Matching and Storage  
7.1 Transfer sample to imaging chamber filled with MACS-R2 for immediate light-sheet or confocal imaging. (Temperature: RT, Time: stable for ≥1 week at 4 ℃ in dark if stored)

**Chosen Method:** FlyClear  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Bruchpilot (BRP/nc82) + Alexa Fluor 488, Synapsin + Alexa Fluor 568]  
**Justification:** FlyClear is an aqueous-based, insect-optimized clearing method specifically validated for Drosophila whole heads and brains (~0.5 mm), preserving fine synaptic ultrastructure with minimal distortion—critical for resolving distinct presynaptic functional domains. It maintains endogenous fluorescence but is fully compatible with immunolabeling using Alexa Fluor dyes. Bruchpilot (nc82) is a well-established marker for the presynaptic active zone in Drosophila, while Synapsin labels synaptic vesicle clusters surrounding the active zone; dual labeling with spectrally distinct Alexa Fluor 488 and 568 enables high-resolution, channel-separated 3D mapping of spatial relationships between these two key presynaptic compartments. FlyClear’s low-toxicity, non-shrinking protocol ensures accurate morphometric analysis across brain regions, and its compatibility with standard confocal/light-sheet imaging after RI matching makes it ideal for this application.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Immunolabeling (post-fixation samples assumed fixed in 4% PFA, washed in PBS)  
1.1 Incubation with blocking solution: 5% normal goat serum (NGS), 0.5% Triton X-100 in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with primary antibodies: mouse anti-Bruchpilot (nc82, 1:50) and rabbit anti-Synapsin (1:200) in blocking solution (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours, gentle agitation)  
1.3 Wash with PBST (0.5% Triton X-100 in PBS): 6 changes over 24 hours (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours per wash)  
1.4 Incubation with secondary antibodies: goat anti-mouse Alexa Fluor 488 (1:400) and goat anti-rabbit Alexa Fluor 568 (1:400) in blocking solution (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours, dark, gentle agitation)  
1.5 Wash with PBST: 6 changes over 24 hours (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours per wash)  

2 Tissue Optical Clearing (FlyClear protocol)  
2.1 Incubation with FlyClear-A: 25% (wt/vol) fructose, 10% (wt/vol) α-thioglycerol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with FlyClear-B: 50% (wt/vol) fructose, 20% (wt/vol) α-thioglycerol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with FlyClear-C: 75% (wt/vol) fructose, 30% (wt/vol) α-thioglycerol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
2.4 Incubation with FlyClear-D: 90% (wt/vol) fructose, 40% (wt/vol) α-thioglycerol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Refractive Index Matching and Mounting  
3.1 Incubation with final RI-matching solution: FlyClear-M (95% wt/vol fructose, 45% wt/vol α-thioglycerol in PBS, RI ≈ 1.45) (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) + Alexa Fluor 647, Neurofilament + Alexa Fluor 568]  
**Justification:** The scientific goal requires simultaneous visualization of mature nerve bundles (cranial/spinal nerves) and delicate early neurites in an ~8–10 mm fixed E12.5 mouse embryo. iDISCO+ is established for this sample tier (T03_SMALL_WHOLE_SAMPLE_1_5MM), provides strong delipidation and deep antibody penetration into dense embryonic tissue, and achieves high transparency rapidly—critical for preserving fine neurite morphology across the entire embryo. Although iDISCO+ quenches endogenous fluorescent proteins, it is fully compatible with Alexa Fluor 568 and 647 conjugates, which offer high photostability, low background, and excellent signal-to-noise for deep imaging. β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) robustly labels all developing neurons including early axons and growth cones, while pan-neurofilament antibodies highlight more mature, bundled axons in cranial and spinal nerves—enabling dual-resolution analysis of neural connectivity establishment. Nuclear counterstains are omitted to avoid masking fine processes.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Bleaching (optional but recommended for endogenous pigment reduction)  
2.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes methanol).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.5 Incubation with 100% PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBT).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.2 Incubation with blocking solution: PBT + 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum + 0.2% (wt/vol) sodium azide.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

5 Primary Antibody Staining  
5.1 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-β-III Tubulin (TUJ1, 1:500) and anti-Neurofilament (pan-NF, 1:300) diluted in blocking solution.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 5 days with gentle agitation)  

6 Washing  
6.1 Incubation with PBT.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.2 Repeat PBT wash.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.3 Repeat PBT wash.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.4 Incubation with PBT + 0.2% (wt/vol) sodium azide.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: overnight)  

7 Secondary Antibody Staining  
7.1 Incubation with secondary antibodies: donkey anti-mouse IgG1 Alexa Fluor 647 (1:300) and donkey anti-rabbit IgG Alexa Fluor 568 (1:300) in blocking solution + 0.2% (wt/vol) sodium azide.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 3 days with gentle agitation)  

8 Post-staining Washes  
8.1 Incubation with PBT.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
8.2 Repeat PBT wash.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
8.3 Repeat PBT wash.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
8.4 Incubation with PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

9 Dehydration (pre-clearing)  
9.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

10 Delipidation  
10.1 Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) in methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.3 Repeat incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

11 Refractive Index Matching  
11.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
11.2 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) DBE in glass vial, protected from light.(Temperature: RT, Time: overnight)  

12 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
12.1 Transfer embryo to imaging chamber filled with fresh DBE; mount in custom holder compatible with light-sheet or confocal microscopy.(Temperature: RT, Time: immediate imaging or store at RT in dark for up to 1 week)

model_response:
**Chosen Method:** FlyClear  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Bruchpilot (BRP/nc82) + Alexa Fluor 647, Synapsin + Alexa Fluor 488]  
**Justification:** FlyClear is an aqueous-based, insect-optimized clearing method specifically validated for Drosophila whole heads and brains (~0.5 mm), preserving fine synaptic ultrastructure with minimal distortion—critical for analyzing spatial organization of synapses. It maintains endogenous fluorescence but, more importantly, supports deep penetration of antibody-conjugated dyes without quenching. Bruchpilot (nc82) is a well-established marker for the presynaptic active zone in Drosophila, while Synapsin labels synaptic vesicle clusters; dual labeling with spectrally distinct Alexa Fluor dyes (AF647 and AF488) enables high-resolution discrimination of active zones versus vesicle pools. FlyClear’s low-toxicity, non-shrinking protocol aligns with the need for accurate 3D morphometry of synaptic domains across brain regions.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Immunolabeling (post-fixation)  
1.1 Incubation with blocking solution: 5% (vol/vol) normal goat serum, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with primary antibodies: mouse anti-Bruchpilot (nc82, 1:50) and rabbit anti-Synapsin (1:200) in blocking solution (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours, gentle agitation)  
1.3 Washing with PBST (0.5% Triton X-100 in PBS): 6 changes over 24 hours (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours per wash)  
1.4 Incubation with secondary antibodies: goat anti-mouse IgG Alexa Fluor 647 (1:400) and goat anti-rabbit IgG Alexa Fluor 488 (1:400) in blocking solution (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours, dark, gentle agitation)  
1.5 Washing with PBST: 6 changes over 24 hours (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours per wash)  

2 Tissue Optical Clearing  
2.1 Incubation with FlyClear Solution A (20% (wt/vol) fructose, 10% (wt/vol) α-thioglycerol in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with FlyClear Solution B (40% (wt/vol) fructose, 20% (wt/vol) α-thioglycerol in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with FlyClear Solution C (63% (wt/vol) fructose, 30% (wt/vol) α-thioglycerol in PBS, RI ≈ 1.45) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

3 Refractive Index Matching and Storage  
3.1 Transfer samples to fresh FlyClear Solution C in glass-bottom imaging chambers (Temperature: RT, Time: ≥1 hour before imaging)  
3.2 Store long-term at 4 ℃ in FlyClear Solution C in the dark (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: indefinite for imaging within 4 weeks)

**Chosen Method:** FlyClear  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Bruchpilot (BRP/nc82)+Alexa Fluor 488, Synapsin+Alexa Fluor 568]  
**Justification:** FlyClear is an aqueous, insect-optimized clearing method specifically validated for Drosophila whole heads and brains, preserving fine synaptic structures while effectively clearing the chitinous cuticle—a key failure point in the user’s prior SeeDB2 attempt. It maintains endogenous fluorescence but is fully compatible with antibody-based labeling using Alexa Fluor dyes, which are stable under its conditions. Bruchpilot (nc82) is the gold-standard marker for Drosophila presynaptic active zones, while Synapsin labels synaptic vesicle clusters, enabling precise dual-channel discrimination of functional synaptic domains. The method avoids organic solvents that cause shrinkage or quenching, supports deep antibody penetration into dense neural tissue with extended incubation, and matches the low-RI requirements of soft neural tissue for high-resolution 3D imaging.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Antibody Labeling (post-fixation, pre-clearing)  
1.1 Incubation with blocking solution: 5% normal goat serum (NGS), 0.5% Triton X-100 in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with primary antibodies: mouse anti-Bruchpilot (nc82, 1:50) and rabbit anti-Synapsin (1:200) in blocking solution (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 72 hours with gentle agitation)  
1.3 Wash with PBST (0.5% Triton X-100 in PBS): 6 changes over 24 hours (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours per wash)  
1.4 Incubation with secondary antibodies: goat anti-mouse Alexa Fluor 488 (1:400) and goat anti-rabbit Alexa Fluor 568 (1:400) in blocking solution (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours with gentle agitation)  
1.5 Wash with PBST: 6 changes over 24 hours (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours per wash)  

2 Tissue Optical Clearing  
2.1 Incubation with FlyClear Solution A (25% w/v fructose, 10% w/v α-thioglycerol, 0.1 M phosphate buffer, pH 7.5) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with FlyClear Solution B (50% w/v fructose, 20% w/v α-thioglycerol, 0.1 M phosphate buffer, pH 7.5) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with FlyClear Solution C (75% w/v fructose, 30% w/v α-thioglycerol, 0.1 M phosphate buffer, pH 7.5) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

3 Refractive Index Matching and Mounting  
3.1 Incubation with final RI-matching medium: FlyClear Imaging Buffer (87% w/v fructose, 35% w/v α-thioglycerol, 0.1 M phosphate buffer, pH 7.5; RI ≈ 1.45) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
3.2 Mount sample in glass-bottom dish or capillary filled with Imaging Buffer, sealed with vacuum grease to prevent evaporation. Store at 4 ℃ in dark until imaging.

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Bruchpilot (BRP/nc82) + Alexa Fluor 647, Synapsin + Alexa Fluor 488]  
**Justification:** The scientific goal requires high-resolution 3D mapping of presynaptic active zones and synaptic vesicle pools in intact Drosophila brains with dense cuticle. iDISCO+ is established for small whole insect samples (~0.5 mm), provides strong delipidation and deep antibody penetration into chitin-rich tissue, and achieves high transparency rapidly. Although it quenches endogenous fluorescent proteins, this is not a limitation here since the labeling strategy uses target-specific primary antibodies against Bruchpilot (a canonical marker of T-bars in Drosophila active zones) and Synapsin (a conserved marker of synaptic vesicle clusters), paired with photostable, iDISCO+-compatible Alexa Fluor dyes (AF647 and AF488). This dual-labeling enables precise spatial correlation between active zones and vesicle domains across brain regions with minimal signal loss during clearing.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Bleaching (optional for pigmented samples)  
2.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes MeOH).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBST).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with PBST + 5% (vol/vol) normal goat serum + 0.3 M glycine.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

5 Primary Antibody Staining  
5.1 Incubation with mouse anti-Bruchpilot (nc82, Developmental Studies Hybridoma Bank, 1:50) and rabbit anti-Synapsin (1:200) diluted in PBST + 5% (vol/vol) normal goat serum + 0.02% (wt/vol) sodium azide.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 5 days, with gentle agitation)  

6 Wash  
6.1 Wash with PBST (3 changes).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)  
6.2 Wash with PBST + 0.2% (wt/vol) heparin.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
6.3 Repeat 6.2 two more times.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours per wash)  

7 Secondary Antibody Staining  
7.1 Incubation with goat anti-mouse IgG conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647 (1:300) and goat anti-rabbit IgG conjugated to Alexa Fluor 488 (1:300) in PBST + 5% (vol/vol) normal goat serum + 0.02% (wt/vol) sodium azide + 0.2% (wt/vol) heparin.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 3 days, with gentle agitation)  

8 Post-staining Wash  
8.1 Wash with PBST + 0.2% (wt/vol) heparin (3 changes).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours per wash)  
8.2 Final wash with PBST.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

9 Dehydration (pre-clearing)  
9.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

10 Delipidation  
10.1 Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) in methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.3 Repeat 10.2 once.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

11 Refractive Index Matching  
11.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
11.2 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) DBE for imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: ≥1 hour)  

12 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
12.1 Transfer sample to glass-bottom imaging dish filled with fresh DBE; seal with coverslip and nail polish to prevent evaporation.(Temperature: RT, Time: immediate imaging or store at RT in dark for ≤1 week)

**Chosen Method:** Ce3D  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Osx (Osterix)+Alexa Fluor 488, Osteocalcin+Alexa Fluor 568]  
**Justification:** The sample is a dense, mineralized hard tissue (P7 mouse cranial suture block), requiring strong clearing with deep antibody penetration while preserving fine 3D morphology to resolve spatial organization of osteolineage cells. Ce3D is an aqueous-based method established for hard tissues (T07 tier), offering excellent preservation of tissue geometry, compatibility with Alexa Fluor dyes, and effective delipidation without hazardous solvents. Osx (Osterix) marks early/mid-stage osteoprogenitors and pre-osteoblasts, while Osteocalcin labels mature osteoblasts/osteocytes—enabling discrimination of differentiation stages across the suture margin, ossification front, and bone plate. Both markers are target-specific for osteolineage cells and compatible with Ce3D’s labeling workflow.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Permeabilization and Blocking  
1.1 Incubation with 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS for permeabilization.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with blocking solution (5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS).(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

2 Primary Antibody Staining  
2.1 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-Osx (1:200) and anti-Osteocalcin (1:200) diluted in blocking solution.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 72 hours)  
2.2 Wash with 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS, 3 changes.(Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours total, 2 hours per wash)  

3 Secondary Antibody Staining  
3.1 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-rabbit IgG (1:400) and Alexa Fluor 568-conjugated anti-mouse IgG (1:400) in blocking solution.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
3.2 Wash with 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS, 3 changes.(Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours total, 2 hours per wash)  

4 Optical Clearing with Ce3D  
4.1 Incubation with Ce3D-A solution (25% (wt/vol) α-thioglycerol, 10% (wt/vol) urea, 10% (vol/vol) glycerol in PBS, pH 8.5).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with Ce3D-B solution (50% (wt/vol) α-thioglycerol, 20% (wt/vol) urea, 20% (vol/vol) glycerol in PBS, pH 8.5).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  

5 Refractive Index Matching  
5.1 Incubation with Ce3D-Matching Solution (80% (wt/vol) α-thioglycerol in PBS, pH 8.5).(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

6 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
6.1 Transfer sample into fresh Ce3D-Matching Solution in glass-bottom imaging chamber.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: until imaging; stable for ≥2 weeks)

**Chosen Method:** Ce3D  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Osx (Osterix)+Alexa Fluor 488, Osteocalcin+Alexa Fluor 568, DAPI]  
**Justification:** Ce3D is an aqueous-based clearing method established for hard tissues like P7 mouse calvaria, offering excellent preservation of tissue morphology with minimal distortion—critical for spatial analysis of suture microarchitecture. It supports deep antibody penetration into mineralized bone and is fully compatible with Alexa Fluor dyes and nuclear counterstains. Osx (Osterix) marks early osteoprogenitors and pre-osteoblasts, while Osteocalcin labels mature, matrix-embedded osteoblasts; dual immunolabeling with spectrally distinct Alexa Fluor conjugates enables precise 3D mapping of lineage progression across suture zones. DAPI provides nuclear context without interfering with target-specific signals, as both markers are protein-based and not DNA-associated.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Immunolabeling (post-fixation, pre-clearing)  
1.1 Incubation with blocking buffer (5% normal donkey serum, 0.5% Triton X-100 in PBS) to reduce non-specific binding. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-Osx (1:200) and anti-Osteocalcin (1:200) diluted in antibody dilution buffer (1% normal donkey serum, 0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS). (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 5 days with gentle agitation)  
1.3 Washing with PBST (0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS), 3 changes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)  
1.4 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-rabbit IgG (1:500) and Alexa Fluor 568-conjugated anti-mouse IgG (1:500) in antibody dilution buffer. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 3 days with gentle agitation)  
1.5 Washing with PBST, 4 changes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)  
1.6 Incubation with DAPI (1 µg/mL in PBS) for nuclear counterstaining. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.7 Final wash with PBS, 2 changes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes per wash)  

2 Tissue Optical Clearing with Ce3D  
2.1 Incubation with Ce3D-A solution (25% (wt/vol) N,N,N′,N′-tetrakis(2-hydroxypropyl)ethylenediamine (THP), 15% (wt/vol) urea, 10% (wt/vol) sucrose in distilled water). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 3 days with gentle shaking)  
2.2 Incubation with Ce3D-B solution (50% (wt/vol) THP, 25% (wt/vol) urea, 10% (wt/vol) sucrose in distilled water). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 4 days with gentle shaking)  

3 Refractive Index Matching and Imaging Preparation  
3.1 Transfer samples to Ce3D-Matching Solution (RI ≈ 1.48; composed of 88% (wt/vol) iodixanol in Ce3D-B base) for final RI homogenization. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
3.2 Mount cleared samples in glass-bottom imaging chambers filled with Ce3D-Matching Solution for light-sheet or confocal microscopy. (Temperature: RT, Time: immediate imaging or storage at 4 ℃ for up to 1 week)
