**Chosen Method:** Ce3D  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Osx (Osterix)+Alexa Fluor 488, Osteocalcin+Alexa Fluor 568]  
**Justification:** P7 mouse calvarial suture tissue is a dense, mineralizing hard tissue requiring strong yet morphology-preserving clearing. Ce3D is an aqueous, high-penetration method established for hard tissues (T07 tier), preserves endogenous fluorescence (though not needed here), and minimizes distortion—critical for spatial mapping of osteolineage cells across suture zones. It effectively reduces bone autofluorescence compared to solvent-based methods like FDISCO or iDISCO+, which often exacerbate background in mineralized matrices. Osx (Osterix) marks early osteoprogenitors/pre-osteoblasts, while Osteocalcin labels mature, matrix-embedded osteoblasts—enabling direct comparison of differentiation stages. Both are target-specific markers validated in bone development. Alexa Fluor 488 and 568 are compatible with Ce3D, offer high signal-to-noise, and avoid spectral overlap with residual bone autofluorescence (typically blue-green). Nuclear counterstains (DAPI/Hoechst) are excluded per marker cautions and to reduce background interference.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Immunolabeling (post-fixation, pre-clearing)  
1.1 Incubation with blocking buffer (5% normal donkey serum, 0.5% Triton X-100 in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-Osx (1:200) and anti-Osteocalcin (1:200) in antibody dilution buffer (1% normal donkey serum, 0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS) (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 72 hours with gentle agitation)  
1.3 Wash with PBST (0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours total, with 3 buffer changes every 2 hours)  
1.4 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-rabbit IgG (1:400) and Alexa Fluor 568-conjugated anti-mouse IgG (1:400) in antibody dilution buffer (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours with gentle agitation)  
1.5 Wash with PBST (0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours total, with 4 buffer changes every 3 hours)  

2 Tissue Optical Clearing with Ce3D  
2.1 Incubation with Ce3D-A solution (25% (wt/vol) α-thioglycerol, 10% (wt/vol) urea, 10% (vol/vol) glycerol in PBS, pH 8.5) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with fresh Ce3D-A solution (same composition) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with Ce3D-B solution (50% (wt/vol) α-thioglycerol, 20% (wt/vol) urea, 20% (vol/vol) glycerol in PBS, pH 8.5) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
2.4 Incubation with fresh Ce3D-B solution (same composition) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  

3 Refractive Index Matching and Storage  
3.1 Incubation with Ce3D-Matching Solution (80% (wt/vol) α-thioglycerol in PBS, pH 8.5) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
3.2 Transfer sample into imaging chamber filled with Ce3D-Matching Solution for light-sheet or confocal microscopy (Temperature: RT, Time: immediate imaging or storage at 4 ℃ for up to 1 week)

**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Osx (Osterix)+Alexa Fluor 488, Osteocalcin+Alexa Fluor 647, Lectin+Alexa Fluor 568]  
**Justification:** FDISCO is a solvent-based clearing method established for hard tissues like postnatal mouse calvarial bone (T07_HARD_TISSUE_BONE_TOOTH_COCHLEA), offering strong delipidation and deep antibody penetration required for dense mineralized tissue. It preserves exogenous fluorophores (Alexa Fluor dyes) while quenching endogenous FPs—ideal since the labeling relies on immunostaining rather than transgenic reporters. The dual-target strategy distinguishes early osteoprogenitors (Osx+) from mature osteoblasts (Osteocalcin+), while Lectin labels vasculature to analyze angiogenesis in suture microenvironments. All chosen fluorophores are compatible with FDISCO per domain records.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Delipidation and Bleaching  
2.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes MeOH).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with permeabilization buffer (0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 10% (vol/vol) DMSO, 0.3 M glycine in PBS).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with blocking buffer (6% (vol/vol) donkey serum, 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 10% (vol/vol) DMSO in PBS).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Primary Antibody Staining  
5.1 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-Osx (1:200), anti-Osteocalcin (1:200), and biotinylated Lectin (1:100) in antibody dilution buffer (3% (vol/vol) donkey serum, 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 10% (vol/vol) DMSO in PBS).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours)  

6 Washing  
6.1 Incubation with washing buffer (0.2% (vol/vol) Tween-20 in PBS) with gentle shaking.(Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours, repeated 3 times with fresh buffer every 2 hours)  

7 Secondary Antibody and Lectin Detection  
7.1 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-rabbit IgG (1:400), Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated anti-goat IgG (1:400), and Alexa Fluor 568-conjugated streptavidin (1:500) in antibody dilution buffer.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours, protected from light)  

8 Post-staining Washes  
8.1 Incubation with washing buffer (0.2% (vol/vol) Tween-20 in PBS).(Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours, repeated 3 times)  
8.2 Incubation with PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

9 Dehydration (Post-staining)  
9.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

10 Clearing and Refractive Index Matching  
10.1 Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) in methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.3 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.4 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) ethyl cinnamate (ECi, Sigma-Aldrich 112372).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

11 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
11.1 Transfer samples to glass vials filled with fresh ethyl cinnamate (ECi) for long-term storage at RT, protected from light.(Temperature: RT, Time: Indefinite until imaging)  
11.2 Mount samples in ECi-filled imaging chambers compatible with light-sheet or confocal microscopy, ensuring no air bubbles.(Temperature: RT, Time: Immediate prior to imaging)

**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [TH + Alexa Fluor 488, CD31 + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** FDISCO is a solvent-based, high-refractive-index clearing method specifically established for dense hard tissues like bone (tier T07_HARD_TISSUE_BONE_TOOTH_COCHLEA). It provides strong delipidation and deep antibody penetration required for intact mouse femur (~15 mm), enabling visualization of fine neural and vascular structures throughout the marrow cavity. Although it quenches endogenous fluorescent proteins, this is not a limitation here since we use immunolabeling with bright, photostable Alexa Fluor dyes. TH (tyrosine hydroxylase) is a specific marker for sympathetic nerve fibers in the bone marrow niche, while CD31 (PECAM1) robustly labels vascular endothelial cells, allowing precise 3D mapping of neuro-vascular spatial relationships. Both primary antibodies are compatible with FDISCO’s organic solvent workflow, and Alexa Fluor 488/647 exhibit excellent stability and signal retention in FDISCO.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Bleaching (optional but recommended for bone autofluorescence reduction)  
2.1 Incubation with chilled 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ + 5 volumes methanol).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration (for immunolabeling)  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 + 10% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum (NDS).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

5 Primary Antibody Incubation  
5.1 Incubation with anti-TH (e.g., rabbit anti-TH, 1:200) and anti-CD31 (e.g., rat anti-CD31, 1:100) diluted in PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 + 5% (vol/vol) NDS.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days with gentle shaking)  

6 Washing  
6.1 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.2 Repeat step 6.1 four more times (total 5 washes).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour each)  

7 Secondary Antibody Incubation  
7.1 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-rabbit IgG (1:400) and Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated anti-rat IgG (1:400) in PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 + 5% (vol/vol) NDS.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 3 days with gentle shaking)  

8 Post-labeling Washing  
8.1 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
8.2 Repeat step 8.1 four more times (total 5 washes).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour each)  

9 Dehydration (post-labeling)  
9.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

10 Delipidation and Clearing  
10.1 Incubation with 1:2 (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) : methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.3 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

11 Refractive Index Matching  
11.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
11.2 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) DBE for long-term storage and imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: ≥1 hour or until imaging)

**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [TH + Alexa Fluor 568, CD31 + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** FDISCO is a solvent-based clearing method established for hard tissues like intact mouse femur (T07_HARD_TISSUE_BONE_TOOTH_COCHLEA), offering strong delipidation and deep antibody penetration required for dense bone and marrow. It preserves exogenous fluorophores (Alexa Fluor dyes) while enabling high refractive index matching for low-scatter 3D imaging of long bones. TH (tyrosine hydroxylase) is a specific marker for sympathetic nerve fibers in the bone marrow niche, and CD31 (PECAM1) robustly labels vascular endothelial networks. Dual labeling with spectrally distinct Alexa Fluor 568 and 647 ensures compatibility with FDISCO’s organic solvent environment and enables precise spatial co-analysis of nerves and vessels across marrow subregions without endogenous FP reliance.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Bleaching (optional, if endogenous pigment present)  
2.1 Incubation with chilled 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in 100% methanol.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration (for immunolabeling)  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with PBS + 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 + 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Primary Antibody Staining  
5.1 Incubation with anti-TH (1:200) and anti-CD31 (1:100) in PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 + 2% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours)  

6 Washing  
6.1 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100.(Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)  
6.2 Repeat wash step 6.1 two more times with fresh buffer each time.(Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours per wash)  

7 Secondary Antibody Staining  
7.1 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 568–conjugated anti-rabbit IgG (1:300) and Alexa Fluor 647–conjugated anti-rat IgG (1:300) in PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 + 2% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  

8 Post-staining Washes  
8.1 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100.(Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)  
8.2 Repeat wash step 8.1 two more times.(Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours per wash)  

9 Dehydration (pre-clearing)  
9.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

10 Delipidation and Clearing  
10.1 Incubation with 1:2 (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) : methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.3 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

11 Refractive Index Matching  
11.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) benzyl alcohol : benzyl benzoate (BABB, 1:2 ratio).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
11.2 Incubation with fresh BABB (1:2).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

12 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
12.1 Transfer sample to glass vial filled with BABB (1:2) and seal with parafilm.(Temperature: RT, Time: Indefinite storage; image within 1 week for optimal signal)

**Chosen Method:** Ce3D  
**Chosen Labeling:** [TH + Alexa Fluor 488, CD31 + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** The problem involves transparentizing intact, mineralized mouse femur—a hard tissue requiring strong yet morphology-preserving clearing. BoneClear caused excessive brittleness during t-BuOH dehydration due to harsh solvent-based delipidation and dehydration steps. Ce3D is an aqueous-based, high-penetration clearing method specifically validated for hard tissues (including bone and marrow), preserves 3D architecture with minimal shrinkage or fragility, and supports deep antibody penetration without organic solvents that compromise structural integrity. TH (tyrosine hydroxylase) is a specific marker for sympathetic nerve fibers in the marrow niche; CD31 robustly labels vascular endothelium, enabling visualization of vessel networks and perivascular spatial relationships. Both primary antibodies are compatible with Ce3D and can be paired with Alexa Fluor 488/647—fluorophores confirmed stable in Ce3D. This combination avoids endogenous FP reliance (which BoneClear quenches anyway) and eliminates brittle t-BuOH steps, directly addressing the sample fragmentation issue.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Immunolabeling (post-fixation)  
1.1 Incubation with blocking buffer (5% normal donkey serum, 0.5% Triton X-100 in PBS) to reduce non-specific binding. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-TH (1:200) and anti-CD31 (1:100) diluted in antibody dilution buffer (1% normal donkey serum, 0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days with gentle agitation)  
1.3 Washing with PBST (0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS), 3 changes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours total, 4 hours per wash)  
1.4 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-rabbit IgG (1:400) and Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated anti-rat IgG (1:400) in antibody dilution buffer. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 3 days with gentle agitation)  
1.5 Washing with PBST, 3 changes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours total, 4 hours per wash)  

2 Tissue Optical Clearing (Ce3D protocol adapted for intact femur)  
2.1 Incubation with Ce3D-A solution (25% (wt/vol) Quadrol, 25% (wt/vol) urea, 10% (wt/vol) sucrose, 0.1 M Tris-HCl pH 7.5) to initiate clearing and enhance antibody penetration. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 3 days with gentle shaking)  
2.2 Washing with PBS, 2 changes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours total)  
2.3 Incubation with Ce3D-B solution (50% (wt/vol) Quadrol, 50% (wt/vol) urea, 0.1 M Tris-HCl pH 7.5) for refractive index homogenization and full transparency. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 4 days with gentle shaking)  

3 Refractive Index Matching and Storage  
3.1 Equilibration in Ce3D-Matching Solution (RI ≈ 1.48; composed of 63% (wt/vol) iodixanol in 0.1 M Tris-HCl pH 7.5, filtered through 0.22 μm) until tissue becomes optically transparent and RI-matched. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
3.2 Transfer samples into imaging chambers filled with fresh Ce3D-Matching Solution for light-sheet or confocal microscopy. Store at 4 ℃ in the dark for up to 2 weeks if not imaged immediately. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: up to 14 days)

**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [TH + Alexa Fluor 568, CD31 + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** FDISCO is a solvent-based, high-refractive-index clearing method specifically established for dense hard tissues like intact mouse bone (T07_HARD_TISSUE_BONE_TOOTH_COCHLEA). It provides strong delipidation and deep antibody penetration required for the ~15 mm mineralized femur, enabling visualization of fine neural and vascular structures throughout the marrow cavity. Although it quenches endogenous fluorescent proteins, our targets—sympathetic nerve fibers (marked by tyrosine hydroxylase, TH) and vascular endothelium (marked by CD31/PECAM1)—are robustly labeled via immunostaining with bright, photostable Alexa Fluor dyes compatible with FDISCO. This dual-labeling strategy directly addresses the scientific goal: mapping spatial relationships between sympathetic innervation (TH+) and vascular architecture (CD31+) in the hematopoietic niche.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

**Chosen Method:** Ce3D  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Phalloidin–Alexa Fluor 647, Myosin VIIa–Alexa Fluor 488, TO-PRO-3]  
**Justification:** The mouse cochlea is a dense, mineralized hard tissue embedded in the otic capsule, requiring a clearing method with strong penetration capability while preserving the delicate spiral architecture and cellular morphology. Ce3D is an aqueous-based, high-penetration clearing protocol established for hard tissues (T07 tier), compatible with both antibody and small-molecule labeling, and causes minimal distortion—critical for accurate 3D hair cell counting across the tonotopic axis. Phalloidin directly labels F-actin in stereocilia bundles of both inner and outer hair cells with high specificity and signal continuity, enabling unambiguous identification of hair cell rows and missing regions without antibodies. Myosin VIIa is a well-validated, hair cell-specific cytosolic marker that complements Phalloidin by labeling the entire hair cell soma, improving segmentation robustness in 3D. TO-PRO-3 provides nuclear counterstain with superior tissue penetration over DAPI/Hoechst in dense samples and is compatible with Ce3D. This combination avoids unnecessary antibody steps for structural elements (Phalloidin suffices for stereocilia) while ensuring cell-type specificity (Myosin VIIa) and nuclear reference (TO-PRO-3), all within a fluorescence-preserving, low-shrinkage clearing framework.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Immunostaining and Cytoskeletal Labeling  
1.1 Incubation with blocking/permeabilization buffer (0.5% Triton X-100, 5% normal donkey serum in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with primary antibody: anti-Myosin VIIa (1:200 in blocking buffer) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
1.3 Washing with PBST (0.1% Tween-20 in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours total, with 3 buffer changes every 2 hours)  
1.4 Incubation with secondary antibody: Alexa Fluor 488–conjugated anti-rabbit IgG (1:400 in blocking buffer) and Phalloidin–Alexa Fluor 647 (1:100 in blocking buffer) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
1.5 Washing with PBST (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours total, with 3 buffer changes every 2 hours)  
1.6 Incubation with TO-PRO-3 (1:1000 in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.7 Final wash with PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

2 Tissue Optical Clearing with Ce3D  
2.1 Incubation with Ce3D-A1 reagent (25% (wt/vol) N,N-bis(2-hydroxyethyl)-2-aminoethanesulfonic acid (BES), 25% (wt/vol) sodium deoxycholate, 30% (wt/vol) urea in distilled water) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with Ce3D-A2 reagent (same composition as A1, freshly prepared) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
2.3 Washing with Ce3D-WB buffer (10% (wt/vol) sucrose, 0.01% (wt/vol) sodium azide in distilled water) (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours, with 2 buffer changes)  

3 Refractive Index Matching  
3.1 Incubation with Ce3D-R1 (RI ≈ 1.45; 47.4% (wt/vol) iohexol, 10% (wt/vol) sorbitol in distilled water) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
3.2 Incubation with Ce3D-R2 (RI ≈ 1.52; 63.2% (wt/vol) iohexol, 10% (wt/vol) sorbitol in distilled water) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

4 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
4.1 Transfer cleared cochlea into fresh Ce3D-R2 in a glass-bottom imaging chamber or matched RI glass vial (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: until imaging)

model_response:
**Chosen Method:** Ce3D  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Phalloidin–Alexa Fluor 488, anti-Myosin VIIa–Alexa Fluor 568, TO-PRO-3]  
**Justification:** The mouse cochlea is a dense, mineralized hard tissue embedded in the otic capsule bone, requiring a clearing method with strong penetration capability while preserving fine F-actin structures and enabling deep antibody access. Ce3D is an aqueous-based, high-penetration clearing protocol established for hard tissues (T07 tier), preserves endogenous and dye-conjugated fluorescence, minimizes morphological distortion of the spiral organ of Corti, and supports robust labeling of both cytoskeletal (F-actin via Phalloidin) and cell-type-specific (Myosin VIIa for hair cells) targets. Phalloidin directly labels F-actin in stereocilia bundles without requiring genetic reporters or secondary amplification, satisfying the requirement to avoid converting structural targets into antibody epitopes. Myosin VIIa is a well-validated, hair cell–specific marker in the cochlea. TO-PRO-3 provides nuclear counterstain compatible with Ce3D and does not interfere with the primary targets. Ce3D’s aqueous nature avoids the shrinkage and distortion risks of solvent-based methods (e.g., FDISCO, uDISCO), critical for accurate hair cell counting across cochlear turns.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Permeabilization and Blocking  
1.1 Incubation with 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS containing 10% (vol/vol) normal goat serum (NGS) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

2 Primary Antibody Staining  
2.1 Incubation with rabbit anti-Myosin VIIa (1:200 dilution) in PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 + 5% (vol/vol) NGS (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days)  
2.2 Wash with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours, repeated 3 times over 24 hours)  

3 Fluorescent Probe Staining (F-actin and Nuclei)  
3.1 Incubation with Phalloidin–Alexa Fluor 488 (1:50 dilution) and TO-PRO-3 (1:1000 dilution) in PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours, protected from light)  
3.2 Wash with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours, repeated 3 times over 24 hours)  

4 Tissue Clearing with Ce3D  
4.1 Incubation with Ce3D Reagent A (25% (wt/vol) α-thioglycerol, 10% (wt/vol) urea, 10% (vol/vol) glycerol in 0.1 M Tris-HCl, pH 8.5) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 3 days)  
4.2 Incubation with Ce3D Reagent B (50% (wt/vol) α-thioglycerol, 20% (wt/vol) urea, 20% (vol/vol) glycerol in 0.1 M Tris-HCl, pH 8.5) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 4 days)  

5 Refractive Index Matching  
5.1 Incubation with Ce3D Mounting Solution (88% (wt/vol) α-thioglycerol in 0.1 M Tris-HCl, pH 8.5, RI ≈ 1.48) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

6 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
6.1 Transfer sample to glass-bottom imaging dish filled with Ce3D Mounting Solution; seal with coverslip using vacuum grease to prevent evaporation (Temperature: 4 ℃, storage until imaging; imaging at RT)
